issues: Voiceover track includes raw AI system prompts read aloud before every section (e.g., 'Say direct, analytical and urgent...').
Narration audio does not match subtitle text due to prompt leaks.
Credibility is heavily compromised by production artifacts.
suggestions: Re-export narration cleanly without prompt directives.
Tighten transitions once the voiceover is fixed.
Ensure subtitle timing aligns precisely with edited audio.

art.summary: Overall execution is clean, visually balanced, and adheres well to brand guidelines. However, several headlines suffer from awkward word wrapping and orphan words ('Now', 'Matters', and split highlights across lines) that diminish the premium feel.

fixes.headline: A Tested Roadmap
fixes.why: Eliminates the generic orphan word 'Matters' on the second line and ties directly to the narration's core message of a structured, tested roadmap.

fixes.headline: Train in Small Groups
fixes.why: 'With Peers' gets awkwardly split across line breaks. 'Train in Small Groups' creates a balanced headline that directly mirrors the narration.

fixes.headline: See Real Progress
fixes.why: Removes the trailing single orphan word 'Now' stranded on the second line for clean typographic hierarchy.

hooks.headline: Hiding Losses Freezes Rating Progress
hooks.line: Hiding your child's lost games does not protect confidence; it quietly freezes their tournament rating.

hooks.headline: Why That 1400 Rating Stalled
hooks.line: Your child doesn't need another opening repertoire—they need to stop running away from their tournament losses.

hooks.headline: Instant Rematches Won't Fix Blunders
hooks.line: Starting a new game immediately after a painful loss does not rebuild confidence; it reinforces bad habits.

hooks.headline: Closing The Screen Costs Points
hooks.line: Closing the laptop right after a painful defeat feels protective, but it silently caps your child's progress.

hooks.headline: Engine Checks Don't Build Masters
hooks.line: Letting an engine highlight red blunders without human guidance only teaches your child to fear their mistakes.

copy.notes: Selected Hook 0 because it directly challenges the emotional instinct of ambitious parents (protecting their child's self-esteem after a defeat) while framing the real cost in terms they track closely: stalled tournament ratings.
